5.1: Arjuna asks again: you praise renunciation of action and also yoga of action — tell me clearly which is better.
5.2: Both lead to the highest good, but of the two, the yoga of action is superior to mere renunciation.
5.3: Know as a perpetual renunciate one who neither hates nor desires; free of the pairs, such a one is easily released.
5.4: Only children speak of knowledge and action as different; one properly established in either gains the fruit of both.
5.5: The state reached by knowledge is reached by action too; one who sees them as one truly sees.
5.6: Renunciation is hard without yoga; the sage established in yoga quickly reaches Brahman.
5.7: One devoted to yoga, pure, self-controlled, seeing the Self in all beings, is not tainted though acting.
5.8: The knower of truth thinks 'I do nothing at all' while seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, moving, sleeping, breathing.
5.9: Speaking, releasing, grasping, opening and closing the eyes — knowing that the senses merely move among their objects.
5.10: One who acts offering all to Brahman, abandoning attachment, is untouched by sin as a lotus leaf by water.
5.11: Yogis act with body, mind, intellect and senses, abandoning attachment, for the purification of the self.
5.12: The united one, abandoning the fruit, attains lasting peace; the disunited, driven by desire and attached to fruit, is bound.
5.13: Renouncing all action mentally, the embodied rests happily in the city of nine gates, neither acting nor causing action.
5.14: The Lord creates neither agency nor actions nor the union with their fruits — it is nature that operates.
5.15: The all-pervading takes on no one's sin or merit; knowledge is veiled by ignorance, and beings are deluded.
5.16: But for those whose ignorance is destroyed by knowledge, that knowledge shines like the sun revealing the Supreme.
5.17: With intellect, mind and whole being absorbed in That, one goes to where there is no return, purified by knowledge.
5.18: The mark of true seeing: the wise look with equal eye on a brahmin, a cow, an elephant, a dog and an outcaste.
5.19: Those whose minds rest in evenness have conquered rebirth here itself; Brahman is flawless and even, and so are they.
5.20: Neither rejoicing in the pleasant nor recoiling from the unpleasant, steady of intellect, undeluded, such a knower rests in Brahman.
5.21: Unattached to external contacts, one finds the joy that is in the Self and enjoys undecaying happiness.
5.22: Pleasures born of contact are wombs of pain, with a beginning and an end; the wise do not delight in them.
5.23: One who can withstand the urge of desire and anger here, before leaving the body, is a yogi and is happy.
5.24: Whose happiness, delight and light are within — that yogi becomes Brahman and attains the peace of Brahman.
5.25: Sages whose sins are destroyed, doubts cut, self-controlled and delighting in the welfare of all beings, attain that peace.
5.26: For the self-controlled, free of desire and anger, who have known the Self, liberation is near on every side.
5.27: Shutting out external contacts, fixing the gaze between the brows, equalising the breath in and out —
5.28: — with senses, mind and intellect controlled, free of desire, fear and anger, such a sage is ever free.
5.29: Knowing Me as the enjoyer of sacrifices, the Lord of the worlds, and the friend of all beings, one attains peace.
